chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Al-Halby, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Regarding the man when he approaches his wife, and he fears that Satan may share/participate with him, he said: He should say 'Bismillah' (In the Name of Allah), and he should seek Refuge with Allah from Satan.
ai.seo_question: What should a man say when approaching his wife to ward off Satan?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes the recitation of 'Bismillah' and seeking refuge in Allah from Satan as a spiritual safeguard against demonic interference during conjugal intimacy. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on transforming natural desires into acts of worship by invoking divine protection, thereby ensuring the act is performed with mindfulness (muraqabah) and purity of intention.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Al Halby who said,

‘Abu Abdllah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding the man, when he goes over to his wife, so he fears the participation of the Satan<sup>la</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should be saying, ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’, and he should be seeking Refuge with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> from the Satan<sup>la</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

About the case of a man who when going to bed with his wife is afraid of Satan’s accompaniment, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that he should say, ‘In the name of Allah’ and seek protection with Allah against Satan.’”
